name: openresto
description: A simple, focused booking management system for restaurants, bars, cafes and more. Set up multiple restaurants per instance, and use your own email address to communicate with your customers. Customers get a simple, cross platform, mobile friendly UI to book tables securely. Self host and cloud friendly.

paragraphs: Documentation · Live Demo - admin: example@example.com / password · resets every 2 hours, feel free to play around and change anything
features: Real-time table holds — when a customer selects a time slot, a 5-minute hold is placed on the specific table via a thread-safe in-memory ConcurrentDictionary. The holdId must be echoed back at booking time, preventing…

Popular-times categorisation — every 30-minute slot is tagged Lunch, Dinner, or Off-Peak using restaurant industry data (Toast/Square/Yelp benchmarks). The frontend groups available slots into labelled pill tabs so…

Paused bookings — admins can halt new reservations until a specific date/time (e.g. during a private event) without touching any configuration files. The availability API checks BookingsPausedUntil before returning…

IANA timezone awareness — all DateTime values are stored in UTC. Restaurant-local open/close hours and slot generation are computed using the restaurant's IANA timezone (America/NewYork, Europe/London, …), so the…
Multi-restaurant support — manage multiple locations from one instance; each has its own tables, sections, hours, timezone, and branding.

requirements.text: Users don't want to install another app, give up their phone number to the cloud, or create another account to remember.
The full self-hosting guide (install, configuration, HTTPS, email, upgrading, troubleshooting) is at docs.openres.to.
Activity trail — every state-changing admin action, plus sign-ins and failed sign-in attempts, is recorded append-only with who did it, when, from which IP, and a before/after diff.

API keys & headless CLI — Owners can mint long-lived, individually revocable API keys (Settings → API Keys), each scoped to exactly the resources it needs (bookings, locations, tables, brand, users, audit, guests) — a key without the guests scope reads bookings with customer identity redacted, so a POS or marketing integration never sees guest contact info. openresto-cli…
